driver.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers how driving ability is checked over time. Every driver eventually needs to assess their own driving skill. Beyond that, the Vehicle Code lets DMV investigate and reexamine any driver whose physical or mental condition, or poor driving record, raises questions about safe operation. We will look at how a driver can assess their own skill, the grounds for a DMV reexamination and the one ground that is never enough, who can refer a driver, how cognitive disorders affect driving, and the range of actions DMV may take after a reexamination.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Assessing yourself","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Recruit a trusted licensed observer.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Listen and apply feedback.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Or take professional lessons.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every driver eventually needs to assess their own driving skill. A driver who is concerned can recruit a trusted licensed observer to ride along, note dangerous behaviors, and suggest fixes. The driver then listens to the feedback and applies it. Another option is to take professional driving lessons instead. So self-evaluation pairs trusted-observer feedback with professional lessons. The point is to find problems early, before they lead to a crash or a referral, and to work on them with help from someone who can see what the driver cannot.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Grounds and referrals","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Conditions or poor records.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Never age alone.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Physicians, officers, family can refer.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Vehicle Code lets DMV investigate and reexamine any driver's ability to operate safely on the basis of physical or mental conditions or a poor driving record, but never on the basis of age alone. Physicians, law enforcement officers, and family members can refer a driver with a physical or mental condition by submitting a completed Request for Driver Reexamination form. So reexamination pairs condition-or-record triggers with the rule that age alone never counts, and the people who most often notice a problem have a formal way to report it to DMV.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Cognitive disorders and outcomes","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Dementia, seizures, strokes, vertigo.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Mild impairment triggers a review.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Outcomes range widely.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Cognitive disorders, from dementia and seizures through brain tumors, Parkinson's disease, strokes, and vertigo, threaten safe driving and can end it. Referrals for even mild impairment trigger a Driver Safety reexamination, with details on the DMV reexamination page. A reexamination may request medical information, hold an in-person or telephone review, require knowledge, vision, or driving tests, issue a limited-term license, immediately suspend or revoke driving for an immediate public threat, or take no action at all. DMV's answers range from medical requests through tests and limited terms to instant suspension or nothing.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Age as the trigger","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: DMV reexamines because of age.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Truth: conditions or records, never age.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. Many people believe DMV reexamines drivers once they reach a certain age. The handbook says the Vehicle Code allows reexamination on the basis of physical or mental conditions or a poor record, never age alone. A second trap is assuming that a reexamination always ends a driver's license. The outcomes range widely: DMV may request medical information, require tests, issue a limited-term license, suspend or revoke only for an immediate public threat, or take no action. A referral starts a review, not an automatic loss of driving.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R01","sec12-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Who can refer a driver?","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R01","sec12-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: which groups does the handbook name as able to refer a driver for reexamination? Settle on your answer. The answer is physicians, law enforcement, and family members. They refer a driver with a physical or mental condition by submitting a completed Request for Driver Reexamination form. If you named all of them, you have the referral rule. Remember that the referral must rest on a condition or a poor record, never on age alone, and that the review that follows can end in anything from tests to no action at all.","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R01","sec12-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Reexamination recap","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Assess yourself; refer when needed.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Never age alone; outcomes vary.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, every driver eventually assesses their own skill, and a concerned driver can recruit a trusted licensed observer or take professional lessons. DMV may reexamine a driver on the basis of physical or mental conditions or a poor record, never age alone. Physicians, law enforcement, and family members can refer drivers with the reexamination request form. Cognitive disorders such as dementia, seizures, Parkinson's disease, and strokes threaten safe driving, and mild-impairment referrals trigger a review. Outcomes range from medical requests and tests to limited-term licenses, immediate suspension, or no action.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04","sec12-F05","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec12-u02","module_id":"sec12-m02","objective_ids":["sec12-u02"],"title":{"text":"Priority It comes with a very short deadline, and missing that deadline leads to suspension. We will look at what the driver must do and how quickly, what kind of evidence the notice rests on, where the notice goes after it is issued, and what happens if the driver does not comply. Because the window is measured in working days and is easy to miss, this is one of the most important rules for any driver who receives a notice.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The five-working-day window","fact_ids":["sec12-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Top box checked.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06"]},{"text":"Contact DMV within five working days.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06"]},{"text":"Otherwise automatic suspension.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"A driver handed a Notice of Priority Reexamination with the top box checked has five working days to contact DMV and start the reexamination process. If the driver does not, driving is automatically suspended. The window is counted in working days, so it is short. The responsibility is the driver's: DMV does not wait for the driver to be ready, and the notice itself sets the clock running. So the top-box check pairs with a five-working-day contact clock, and automatic suspension is the penalty for missing it. Missing the window means automatic suspension.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What the notice rests on","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Incapacity evidence at a violation.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},{"text":"Driver gets a copy.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},{"text":"Officer faxes and mails it to DMV.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"A priority notice rests on evidence of incapacity seen at a Vehicle Code violation, suggesting the driver cannot operate a vehicle without danger. The driver receives a copy of the notice, and the officer faxes and mails the notice to the Driver Safety Office. Non-compliance notices order the driver to contact DMV under the Vehicle Code, and missing the five-working-day window suspends driving until a satisfactory reexamination. So incapacity evidence at a violation starts the process, the officer handles the paperwork, and the driver's job is to make contact in time.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Waiting for DMV to call","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: DMV will reach out.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F08"]},{"text":"Truth: the driver must contact DMV.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. A driver who receives a priority notice may assume DMV will reach out to schedule the reexamination. The handbook puts the duty on the driver: contact DMV within five working days and start the process, or driving is automatically suspended. A second trap is treating the suspension as permanent and giving up. Missing the window suspends driving until a satisfactory reexamination, so the path back is to complete the reexamination. Either way, acting within the five working days is far better than losing driving and having to recover it.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec12-F08","sec12-F06","sec12-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"The contact window was missed.","fact_ids":["sec12-F08","sec12-F06","sec12-F07"]},{"text":"What happens?","fact_ids":["sec12-F08","sec12-F06","sec12-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: what happens to a driver who does not contact DMV within five working days after a priority reexamination notice? Choose your answer. The answer is that driving is suspended until a satisfactory reexamination. The suspension is automatic once the window passes. If you answered suspension until a satisfactory reexamination, you have the rule. Remember the sequence: the officer issues the notice based on incapacity evidence at a violation, the driver gets a copy, and the driver has five working days to contact DMV.","fact_ids":["sec12-F08","sec12-F06","sec12-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Priority notice recap","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Five working days to contact DMV.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},{"text":"Missed window means suspension.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, a driver handed a Notice of Priority Reexamination with the top box checked has five working days to contact DMV and start the reexamination process, or driving is automatically suspended. The notice rests on evidence of incapacity seen at a Vehicle Code violation suggesting the driver cannot operate without danger. The driver receives a copy, and the officer faxes and mails the notice to the Driver Safety Office. Missing the window suspends driving until a satisfactory reexamination. Next, we look at the restrictions DMV can place on a license.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec12-u03","module_id":"sec12-m03","objective_ids":["sec12-u03"],"title":{"text":"License restrictions","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Restrictions let drivers keep driving within their abilities instead of losing their license.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"After a reexamination, an examiner finds that Rosa sees poorly at night but drives safely in daylight.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Restrictions keep drivers within their abilities, rooted in examiner findings, and may include time limits like no night driving.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Rosa's license is restricted to daytime driving, so she can keep driving within her abilities.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking seniors automatically get license restrictions.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11"]},"correction":{"text":"No restrictions target seniors specifically; every restriction answers a condition, never an age.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Restrictions fit the condition, not the birthday.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Name one kind of restriction DMV can place on a license.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"For example, hand controls, no night driving, corrective lenses, or an outside mirror.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"Restrictions may require devices, time-and-place limits, eyeglasses or contacts, or added equipment like outside mirrors.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Driving within your abilities","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Why restrictions exist.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]},{"text":"What they can require.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers license restrictions. A restriction is a way to keep a driver on the road safely by matching their driving to their abilities. Restrictions may be imposed by DMV or required by law, and they must always be reasonable and necessary. We will look at what restrictions are based on, the kinds of restrictions that can be placed on a license, and the important rule that no restriction targets age. Understanding restrictions helps you see that a reexamination often leads to tailored limits rather than an end to driving.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Why and how restrictions apply","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Keep drivers within their abilities.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Reasonable and necessary.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Rooted in examiner findings.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"License restrictions keep drivers operating within their abilities. They may be imposed by DMV or required by law, and they are always reasonable and necessary. Every restriction is rooted in an examiner's findings and recommendations. So a restriction is not a punishment; it is a fit between what the driver can safely do and what the license allows. Because restrictions rest on what the examiner actually finds, drivers of the same age can end up with very different restrictions, or none at all, depending on their own abilities.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Kinds of restrictions","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vehicle devices like hand controls.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Time and place limits.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Glasses, contacts, outside mirrors.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Restrictions can take several forms. They may require vehicle devices, such as hand controls. They may set time-and-place limits, such as no night driving or no freeway driving. They may require eyeglasses or corrective contact lenses. Or they may require added equipment, such as outside mirrors. No restrictions target seniors specifically; every restriction answers a condition, never an age. So restrictions pair ability-matching with condition-only tailoring across devices, limits, glasses, and mirrors, each chosen to address what the examiner found.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":32,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The age assumption","fact_ids":["sec12-F11","sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: seniors get automatic limits.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11","sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Truth: restrictions answer conditions only.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11","sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. Many people assume older drivers automatically receive license restrictions. The handbook says no restrictions target seniors specifically; every restriction answers a condition, never an age. A second trap is thinking restrictions are arbitrary. They must be reasonable and necessary and are always rooted in examiner findings and recommendations. So if a driver of any age receives a restriction such as no night driving or a requirement for corrective lenses, it is because of something the examiner found about that driver, not because of a birthday.","fact_ids":["sec12-F11","sec12-F09","sec12-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-R02","sec12-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Name a restriction.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-R02","sec12-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: name one kind of restriction DMV can place on a license. Make your choice. Possible answers include vehicle devices such as hand controls, time-and-place limits such as no night or freeway driving, eyeglasses or corrective contacts, or added equipment such as outside mirrors. If you named any of these, you have the idea. Remember that every restriction answers a condition found by an examiner, never an age, and that restrictions are always reasonable and necessary to keep the driver within their abilities.","fact_ids":["sec12-F10","sec12-R02","sec12-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Section wrap-up","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Restrictions match abilities.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Conditions, never age.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish this section, license restrictions keep drivers operating within their abilities. They may be imposed by DMV or required by law, are always reasonable and necessary, and are rooted in examiner findings and recommendations. They may require devices like hand controls, time-and-place limits like no night or freeway driving, eyeglasses or contacts, or added equipment like outside mirrors. No restriction targets seniors; every restriction answers a condition. Together with self-assessment, reexamination, and priority notices, restrictions round out how driver safety is kept in check.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11","sec12-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]}]}
